# 03. Information Architecture

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Make pages, navigation, URLs, and content relationships easy to understand for users, crawlers, translators, and maintainers.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A complete sitemap listing every public page, utility page, legal page, localized page, content archive, and error page.
- [ ] A URL policy for slugs, trailing slashes, capitalization, language folders, location folders, blog paths, and redirects.
- [ ] A navigation model for primary navigation, secondary navigation, footer navigation, breadcrumbs, and contextual cross-links.
- [ ] A page-type inventory covering homepage, service, portfolio, case study, article, category, location, contact, legal, and error states as needed.
- [ ] A canonical page map that identifies the preferred URL for every content item.
- [ ] A content hierarchy for each template: page purpose, H1, primary sections, proof blocks, CTA, related content, and metadata.
- [ ] A taxonomy plan for blog categories, tags, topics, industries, services, locations, and languages where relevant.
- [ ] An internal linking standard that defines which pages must link to which related conversion or authority pages.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Users must be able to predict what they will find from link labels before clicking.
- [ ] Navigation must expose business-critical pages without overwhelming users with every page.
- [ ] URL paths must be stable, readable, lowercase, hyphenated, and free of implementation artifacts.
- [ ] Each page must have one clear parent or collection relationship unless it is intentionally standalone.
- [ ] Important pages must not be orphaned from navigation, footer, sitemap, and contextual links.
- [ ] Breadcrumbs must reflect the real hierarchy and not invent relationships for SEO appearance.
- [ ] Localized pages must map equivalent content relationships across languages or declare intentional gaps.
- [ ] Archive and tag pages must have enough unique value to be indexable; thin archive pages must be noindexed or omitted.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check for duplicate page purposes, duplicate slugs, inconsistent labels, and conflicting navigation paths.
- [ ] Check that all internal links resolve on a static host with case-sensitive file paths.
- [ ] Check that footer navigation includes essential trust, contact, legal, and conversion support links.
- [ ] Check that 404 pages guide users to meaningful recovery paths.
- [ ] Check that sitemap.xml and human navigation agree on indexable page URLs.
- [ ] Check that canonical URLs, hreflang URLs, and Open Graph URLs use the final production domain.
- [ ] Check that page depth does not bury priority pages behind unnecessary intermediary pages.
- [ ] Check that users can reach key conversion pages from any page within one or two meaningful clicks.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid navigation labels that are clever but unclear.
- [ ] Avoid URL structures copied from no-code exports, temporary folders, file names, dates, or campaign language.
- [ ] Avoid relying on JavaScript-only navigation for essential page discovery.
- [ ] Avoid duplicate content caused by multiple equivalent URLs without canonicals.
- [ ] Avoid empty categories, tag sprawl, and location pages with swapped city names only.
- [ ] Avoid deep dropdowns that are hard to use by keyboard, touch, or screen readers.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The site architecture must feel obvious to first-time visitors and predictable to returning users.
- [ ] Search engines must be able to crawl all indexable pages from static links.
- [ ] The IA must support future content additions without changing established URL rules.
- [ ] Every structural choice must reduce cognitive load or improve findability.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use internal link audits to flag broken links, orphan pages, duplicate titles, duplicate canonical targets, and missing sitemap entries.
- [ ] Use the fix script to generate sitemap.xml and robots.txt from the static HTML inventory.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Site structure has a clear hierarchy, intuitive page names, distinct page roles, logical grouping, accessible priority pages, and restrained main navigation.
- [ ] Home, about, services, solutions, work/cases/portfolio, insights/resources, contact, legal, sitemap, privacy, accessibility, cookie, 404, and thank-you pages exist where planned.
- [ ] Navigation supports forward, backward, and sideways movement with consistent labels, active states, footer completion, contextual links, breadcrumbs where useful, and mobile-specific simplicity.
- [ ] URLs are short, readable, lowercase, stable, crawlable, canonicalized, free from temporary labels, and consistent across language, blog, portfolio, service, and product paths.
- [ ] No important page is orphaned, buried, duplicated, cannibalized, discoverable only by JavaScript, or excluded from sitemap/footer/navigation without a documented reason.
- [ ] Footer structure supports discovery, contact, legal trust, SEO, and recovery without becoming spammy or visually dominant.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
